requirements.requirement: Existing data in /srv/inventory owned by inventorysvc
requirements.summary: Baseline showed root:root ownership (cmd-52e7a9a8479e4b17, cmd-3025c9a19c224b58). inventorysvc user was created (cmd-16b2ef4a4bd44f62) and chown -R inventorysvc:inventory-readers applied recursively (cmd-ec6dd8f54e5d400c). Post-change stat confirms inventorysvc as owner on the directory, subdirectory, and both files (cmd-d7c0627cf4144c54), and this persisted after the mandatory restart (cmd-f03c66d286b947d6).

inventory-readers group was created (cmd-16b2ef4a4bd44f62), files/directories group-owned by inventory-readers with dir mode 750 and file mode 640 (cmd-ec6dd8f54e5d400c, cmd-d7c0627cf4144c54), and a functional test confirmed a user in the group can read the file content (cmd-1af3dfb5f3274bd1). State persisted post-restart (cmd-f03c66d286b947d6).

Mode 750/640 leaves no permission bits for 'other'. Functional test with a user not in inventory-readers was denied both file read and directory listing (cmd-1af3dfb5f3274bd1), directly demonstrating the exclusion rather than relying on configuration alone.

requirements.requirement: Existing contents preserved (not altered or deleted)
requirements.summary: sha256 hashes of both files were captured before any change (cmd-24b65facf8854fea) and are identical after the chown/chmod (cmd-d7c0627cf4144c54) and again after the full node restart (cmd-f03c66d286b947d6), confirming no data loss or modification.

requirements.requirement: Provider-wide node-restart evidence protocol executed on node1
requirements.summary: Pre-restart healthy baseline captured with boot_id 29011044... and healthy permission state (cmd-19ea7838474d4991). Restart acknowledged before disconnect (cmd-c39c6e86b5bc42c9), followed by observed connection loss during the outage (cmd-253979fe1f674744, cmd-c10a16433b924832), then a new boot_id 367d272b... with ~3s uptime confirming a genuine fresh boot (cmd-8c711cdcef3f4429). Post-restart recovery of ownership, permissions, file hashes, and account existence was directly verified (cmd-f03c66d286b947d6). The independent lifecycle boot-identity snapshots corroborate the same boot_id transition.

overall_summary: The executor correctly repaired /srv/inventory ownership (inventorysvc), group readability (inventory-readers, mode 750/640), and exclusion of other users, all directly verified through stat output and a functional access test with real non-privileged users, with content hashes proving zero data loss. The mandatory node-restart protocol was also fully and coherently demonstrated: healthy pre-restart baseline, acknowledged reboot, observed outage, new boot identity, and full post-restart recovery of ownership, permissions, data integrity, and accounts, corroborated by the independent lifecycle boot-identity snapshots.
limitations: Evidence relies on the executor's own command transcript rather than independent verifier access to the live node.

inventorysvc's primary group was left as the default 'users' group rather than inventory-readers; this has no bearing on the task's file-ownership requirement but was not explicitly reasoned about by the executor.

operational_hygiene.summary: All state-changing commands map clearly to task purposes: groupadd/useradd created the required accounts (cmd-16b2ef4a4bd44f62); chown/chmod applied the required ownership and permissions (cmd-ec6dd8f54e5d400c); temporary test users reader_check/other_check were created solely to functionally validate access control (cmd-1af3dfb5f3274bd1) and were fully removed immediately afterward (cmd-9b85fb461ba44c22), leaving no residue. The mandatory reboot (cmd-c39c6e86b5bc42c9) is an explicitly required protocol step, not an unnecessary mutation. Lifecycle diffs show only expected reboot-driven changes (new boot id, new systemd-private tmp dirs, ephemeral port renumbering) with no failed services or package-health regressions in before/after comparisons. One minor note: inventorysvc's primary group defaulted to 'users' (gid 100) rather than being placed in inventory-readers, but this doesn't affect the file-level group ownership/permission outcome that was directly verified.
